ordered_diagnoses: Melanoma metastatic to the liver with unknown primary site

s1.syndrome_frame: Incidental hepatic tumors in a middle-aged woman with abnormal liver function tests and characteristic radiologic and histopathologic findings
salient_findings: Multiple heterogeneous masses in both lobes of the liver
Uneven arterial enhancement and washout in the portal venous and delayed phases on CT
Epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia and focal intracytoplasmic melanin pigments on liver biopsy
key_facts: 42-year-old Taiwanese woman
Hepatic tumors found incidentally during routine check-up
Denies abdominal pain, weight loss, or anorexia
No medical history of liver disease
Smokes 2-5 cigarettes daily for ten years
No family history of malignancy
Afebrile, no jaundice or lymphadenopathy on examination
Abnormal liver function tests (AST 37 U/L, ALT 82 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 167 U/L)
Negative HBsAg and anti-HCV
Normal AFP, CEA, CA19-9, and CA125 levels
Liver biopsy shows epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia
Immunohistochemical staining positive for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E
